system: You are an analyst who writes clear, concise business reports.
prompt:
Write a report of 5 to 8 sentences for investors at Orbitly on business metrics for January 2026, based on this data.

Company: Orbitly
Period: January 2026

Data:
- Net revenue retention (NRR): 85%
- Net revenue retention (NRR) in the previous month: 88%
- Change in net revenue retention (NRR) vs the previous month, in percentage points: -3 pp
- Trial-to-paid conversion: 5.7%
- Change in trial-to-paid conversion vs the previous month, in percentage points: 0.5 pp
- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR): 371,288 GBP
- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) in the previous month: 348,903 GBP
- Change in monthly recurring revenue (MRR) vs the previous month: 6.4%
- Monthly churn: 0.6%
- Monthly churn in the previous month: 0.5%
- Change in monthly churn vs the previous month, in percentage points: 0.1 pp
- New customers: 47 customers
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC): 2,208 GBP
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC) in the previous month: 2,079 GBP
- Change in customer acquisition cost (CAC) vs the previous month: 6.2%
- Verdict on the change in monthly churn vs the previous month, in percentage points: stability

Write only the report, in prose, with no headings or lists.
raw: January 2026 saw Monthly Recurring Revenue climb 6.4 % to £371,288, reflecting solid organic growth from the prior month’s £348,903. Net Revenue Retention slipped to 85 % from 88 %, a 3‑percentage‑point decline that signals modest revenue contraction among existing accounts. Conversely, the trial‑to‑paid conversion rate improved by 0.5 percentage points, reaching 5.7 % and indicating more effective onboarding of new users. Monthly churn edged up to 0.6 % from 0.5 %, a marginal 0.1‑point increase that the team characterises as stable rather than alarming. The company added 47 new customers in the period, though the Customer Acquisition Cost rose 6.2 % to £2,208, suggesting higher spending to secure each new account. Overall, the revenue expansion outpaces the slight churn and acquisition cost uptick, positioning Orbitly for continued incremental growth in the coming months.
